# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||

    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:

      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}

      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'

Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …
