Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

The knob comment must be updated to explain: opt-in transition to the rework status for projects whose bounce-back leaves the ticket in a queued status; the written status is the ACTUAL phase (In Rework), never the stale dev-phase status.

Renaming config keys is risky (it's a documented public config knob: configLoader.js line 43-47, docs). Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted …

arguments.content:
# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `github_get_pr_diff_text` is invoked from `js/common/scm.js` with the argument name `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing), but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch fails on every single call and a multi-step fallback chain silently does the real work.

**Root cause**: `js/common/scm.js`, GitHub provider, two call sites pass the wrong argument casing:

- `getDiffText()` (line ~193): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: String(prId) })`
- `getPrDiff()` (line ~267): `github_get_pr_diff_text({ workspace, repository, pullRequestID: prIdStr })`

The tool schema for `github_get_pr_diff_text` requires `pullRequestId` (camelCase — the casing used by every other `github_*` tool call site in the repo). With the required argument missing under its expected name, the host callback rejects the call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`) — observed 4/4 failing in fa run 37806292238. Each failure is masked by the `getPrDiff` fallback chain (legacy `github_get_pr_diff` → local `git diff`), so the pipeline "works" while the primary path fails 100% of the time.

Note: the **legacy** `github_get_pr_diff` fallback (line ~280) keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's schema genuinely uses `pullRequestID` (verified against the runtime tool catalog), and a unit test pins it.

**Impact**: Every diff fetch takes the slow fallback path (extra tool calls + local git diff); when the working tree is not a faithful merge state, the fallback can produce wrong or empty diffs for review-comment anchoring. A hidden 100%-failure path that the fallback papers over (same failure shape as the #799 "no code changes required" incident).

**Fix approach**:

1. **AC1** — rename the argument to `pullRequestId` at both `github_get_pr_diff_text` call sites in `js/common/scm.js`; pin the exact arg name with a unit test.
2. **AC2** — keep/strengthen the call-count test: when `github_get_pr_diff_text` succeeds, exactly 1 tool call happens and no fallback (legacy tool, `github_get_pr`, local git) is exercised.
3. **AC3 log-hygiene bundle** (same forensic review):
   - (a) `js/common/gitOps.js` `detectMergeConflicts()` unconditionally logs `No merge conflicts — base branch changes staged` even when the branch was already up to date and the merge staged nothing. Fix: detect the no-op merge (`git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after the clean merge) and log an accurate line for the up-to-date case.
   - (b) `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` — the opt-in "mark active during rework" transition (`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment`) writes `statuses.IN_DEVELOPMENT`, the stale dev-phase status, during a rework leg. Fix: write the actual transition target `statuses.IN_REWORK` and log it accordingly.
   - (c) `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` logs the questions-fetch failure as `console.error('Failed to fetch questions, continuing without file:', fetchError)` — the Error object renders as `{}` in the GraalJS host log, swallowing the cause. Fix: log the error message/content.
   - (d) `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — `removeConfiguredLabels()` is the single removal site for `agent:rework` in the rework post-action; the main success path removes the configured rework labels exactly once. Covered by a unit test pinning exactly one `agent:rework` removal per successful rework completion (call-count test), so any future double-removal fails the suite.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix attempt for gh-802.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED: update `test_githubHelpers.js` diff-text pins to expect `pullRequestId` (fails against current code); add wording/count tests for AC3(a)–(d) in the touched files' suites (`test_gitOps.js`, `test_preCliReworkSetup.js`, `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js`/equivalent, `test_pushReworkChanges.js`).
- GREEN: minimal fixes in `scm.js`, `gitOps.js`, `preCliReworkSetup.js`, `fetchQuestionsToInput.js`.
- REG: full `run_all.json` green.
